tier_reason: tally is a command-line program with no HTTP surface. The trial reaches `renders` only when `app_url` answers an HTTP request and a browser screenshot of it succeeds, and there is no page to point it at: cmd/tally/main.go reads stdin or a file argument, prints to stdout, and exits. Everything this repo contains does build and test, so build_and_test is the ceiling here rather than a shortfall.

static_checks.name: gofmt
static_checks.command: mkdir -p .bsf-reports && gofmt -l . | awk 'BEGIN{printf "{\"version\":\"2.1.0\",\"$schema\":\"https://json.schemastore.org/sarif-2.1.0.json\",\"runs\":[{\"tool\":{\"driver\":{\"name\":\"gofmt\",\"informationUri\":\"https://pkg.go.dev/cmd/gofmt\",\"rules\":[{\"id\":\"gofmt\",\"shortDescription\":{\"text\":\"File is not gofmt-formatted\"}}]}},\"results\":["; n=0} {sub(/^\.\//,""); if(n++) printf ","; printf "{\"ruleId\":\"gofmt\",\"level\":\"warning\",\"message\":{\"text\":\"%s is not gofmt-formatted; run gofmt -w %s\"},\"locations\":[{\"physicalLocation\":{\"artifactLocation\":{\"uri\":\"%s\"},\"region\":{\"startLine\":1}}}]}", $0, $0, $0} END{printf "]}]}\n"}' > .bsf-reports/gofmt.sarif
static_checks.why: gofmt ships with the Go toolchain this repo already requires, and .factory/rules/go.yaml detects it from go.mod alone, but the factory's static gate does not run it: for a Go repo it runs `go vet` natively and nothing else. Formatting drift is therefore the one checkable Go defect class that nothing in the factory would otherwise count. The check is binary per file, which is what gofmt means, so each unformatted file is exactly one `gofmt` finding at line 1 and the per-file ratchet reads naturally. staticcheck, the other linter in the rule pack, is deliberately not here: its detect list is .golangci.yml / staticcheck.conf and this repo has neither, so adding it would be adding a tool the repo does not use.

dropped.why: That step provisions a toolchain on a GitHub runner; the sandbox already has Go on PATH (go1.26.11 here, satisfying the `go 1.22` line in go.mod), so pinning it again is CI plumbing rather than something the app needs installed.

dropped.what: The "The binary totals a timesheet" step: `go run ./cmd/tally` piped a two-line timesheet and grepped for '^site *1h30m$'
dropped.why: Not dropped as unnecessary — it is the right smoke check, and it is carried into the runbook's Verify section and into capabilities.exercised instead. It is kept out of commands.test so that a failure there reads as "the binary misbehaved" rather than "go test failed".
These are the factory's own machinery operating on this repo, not part of the application under test. Building or running them is not what verifying a change to tally means.

The rule pack detects staticcheck from .golangci.yml, .golangci.yaml or staticcheck.conf and this repo has none of them, so it is a checker the repo does not use; installing it would also make every static gate compile a tool from the module proxy before it could check anything. gofmt and the factory's built-in `go vet` are both already here.

not_exercised.what: Anything a browser would see — a rendered page, a screenshot, a DOM assertion
not_exercised.why: The repo has no web surface at all: no server, no templates, no HTTP handler. This is the fixture's stated point, not a gap in the sandbox.

not_exercised.what: Automated test coverage of cmd/tally/main.go — argument handling, the stdin-vs-file choice, the `%-20s` output column, and the exit codes

Since this amendment it is at least *counted*: it is in the lcov report at 0%, so a PR that changes cmd/tally/main.go now measures 0% diff coverage and fails the 80% gate until a test is added alongside it, rather than reporting 'nothing measurable' and passing. The behaviour itself is reachable only by running the binary and reading its output, which verification here does by hand.

not_exercised.what: Any Go analysis deeper than `go vet` and gofmt — staticcheck's SA/ST/S checks, errcheck, ineffassign and the rest of a golangci-lint suite
not_exercised.why: The repo configures none of them: there is no .golangci.yml, no staticcheck.conf, and ci.yml runs only `go vet` and `go test`. Installing one would be adding a tool the repo does not use, so the static gate counts `go vet` (built into the factory) and `gofmt` (declared here) and nothing else. A later decision to adopt golangci-lint would be an amendment, not a silent addition.

not_exercised.what: Branch coverage, and the distinction between a line that ran once and a line that ran in every case that matters
not_exercised.why: Go's coverage is statement-based. The lcov report maps each covered block onto the lines it spans, so a line inside a multi-line block counts as covered when the block ran at all. That is the most Go reports; it is not a sandbox limitation that could be fixed here.

not_exercised.what: Behaviour on any OS other than linux/amd64, and on non-UTF-8 or very large timesheets
not_exercised.why: The trial runs a single Linux runner, and bufio.Scanner's default 64KiB line limit is never approached by the inputs tried here. Nothing in the repo asks for either, so no attempt was made to cover them.

Amendment. Read amend.json — one report, from the owner: the coverage gate reports no coverage report on every PR so diff coverage is never measured, and the static gate may be checking nothing. Rather than guess at what the gates read, unpacked .factory/bin/runner.tgz and read the consuming code: readCoverage/fromLcov, diffCoverage, runCoverageGate, runStaticTools, runSarifCheck, countSarif, runTestsGate, closedEnv/shellBase, and the trial's checks loop.
episode.observed: Four facts settled the design. (1) `bsf gates coverage` only *reads* the report; it is `bsf gates tests` that runs `commands.build && commands.coverage`, and only because factory.yaml has `existing_ci.test_check: null` — with a test_check set it would short-circuit on ci.yml's result and never write a report. (2) fromLcov reads only SF/LF/LH per record, and diffCoverage sums whole-file covered/total over the changed files, so per-file totals are what matter and a changed file absent from the report yields `null` diff coverage, which the gate then treats as 100%. (3) runStaticTools already runs `go vet` natively whenever go.mod exists, so the static gate was *not* checking nothing here — declaring go vet again would double-count the same findings. (4) A declared static check is judged only on whether its SARIF exists and parses, and the trial silently drops one that does not, so the command must write a valid SARIF even when it finds nothing.
episode.changed: Scoped the amendment: add commands.coverage + coverage_report, and add exactly one static check — a Go checker the factory does not already run. Kept every existing command, the tier, the empty env/services/stubs and the egress list untouched.

episode.tried: Built the coverage command. First tried the obvious `go test -coverprofile=... ./...`, then compared it with `-coverpkg=./...`. Converted Go's coverprofile to lcov with an awk program embedded in the command itself, because nothing written into the repo during setup is kept, so the command has to be self-contained. Ran the whole thing under the closed environment (PATH, HOME, TMPDIR, LANG, CI only).
episode.observed: Without -coverpkg the profile contains only internal/tally/tally.go, because cmd/tally has no test binary of its own — so a PR touching cmd/tally/main.go would have hit diffCoverage's `total === 0` path, scored `null`, and been waved through at 100%. With `-coverpkg=./...` both files appear: internal/tally/tally.go 35/40 lines and cmd/tally/main.go 0/18, 60.3% overall. The awk converter emits TN/SF/DA/LF/LH/end_of_record with repo-relative paths (the module path from `go list -m` is stripped off the profile's import-path-qualified names, which is what fromLcov's rel() needs). Exit 0, no network.
episode.changed: Set commands.coverage to `go vet ./... && mkdir -p coverage && go test -covermode=count -coverpkg=./... -coverprofile=coverage/cover.out ./... && awk ... > coverage/lcov.info`, and coverage_report to coverage/lcov.info as lcov. `go vet` is kept at the front so the tests gate, which runs this command *instead of* commands.test, stays exactly as strict as commands.test is.

episode.tried: Chose and proved the static check. Compared .factory/rules/go.yaml's four tools against what runStaticTools already runs: go-vet is native to the factory, gitleaks runs as a pinned action in CI and needs .gitleaks.toml (absent), staticcheck's detect list is .golangci.yml / .golangci.yaml / staticcheck.conf (all absent), gofmt's detect is go.mod alone and nothing in the factory runs it.
